div.font: Appendix D (2/5)
Purpose, Explanation, and Arbitrariness

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 796px; height: 1px; padding-top: 98px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.style: font-size: 16px;

b.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); text-align: left;
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 12px;

div.font: - "Purpose is emergent without needing any real will behind it."
- "Purpose can be purely functional - no mind is required."
- The concept of "purpose" does not imply an agent with a will: things can have functions (or be goal-directed) without being intended by anyone.
- As a result, inferring a "will beyond reality" from what is only perceived "purpose" is a category error: it invalidly requires "will" when only "purpose" is known.

- Either:
- The claim that "purpose only comes from my own will" - which means that "there are no external wills (that we can know of) that affect reality".
- The claim that "some purposes don't have wills".
- The claim that "purpose is just in the mind" - or "purpose itself doesn't ontologically exist" - thus eliminating the requirement for "will" altogether.
- The claim that "reality doesn't need 'purpose' to explain it" - thus eliminating the requirement for "will" altogether.

font.b: How the Project Addresses These Commitments

div.font: - "There are no external wills

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - Firstly, we define "causation" as the relationship between "my will" and certain "changes in reality" (ex. how your body moves, new thoughts that emerge, etc.) - and this is the only [phenomenological] grounding/observation we have for the concept.

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - In other words, our direct observation of "cause" depends on a "will" and an "effect".

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: Note that we are not [phenomenologically] aware of any will besides our own.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - Secondly, we observe "cause-and-effect" occurrences in reality (ex. water causing plants to grow, planets orbiting the sun because of gravity, other people reacting to what happens around them, etc.).

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - As a result, we have two options:

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - Because we do not observe a "will" behind "cause-and-effect" occurrences, there must not be one - or, we can never know if there is one. These depend on the claim that "perception = reality", as if we can't perceive an external will, then it cannot exist, nor can we even arrive at knowing if one does exist.

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - Because we have direct access to the "behind the scenes" of our own "cause-and-effect" occurrences, then there must be a "will" behind all others.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - This project rejects the "perception = reality" claim (see the Discovering Reality section) - making the "existence of an external will" claim a better fit with our observations.

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - If you reject the existence of an external will, then you either accept that "perception = reality" or reject that "cause-and-effect" occurrences exist (or can even be observed) - meaning that you will need to define some other explanation that is a better fit with our observations of reality.

div.font: - "Some purposes don't have wills."
- This requires an epistemological distinction between a "purpose with will" and "purpose

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: without will" - meaning, you must have observed some purpose that you know lacks a will.

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: If this observation reduces to "perception = reality", see the response to the previous commitment.

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - Otherwise, this needs to be proven: what observation (ie. source of information) did you make where you noticed that some purposes don't have wills?

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.font: - See the third objection.
- "Reality doesn't need 'purpose' to explain it."
- See the fourth objection.

div.font: - "There is no purpose to the universe."
- "Everything is arbitrary/meaningless."
- "Purpose is a human illusion."
- The universe - including human existence - doesn't have a "purpose", for there is no ultimate, conscious will that could have caused its existence.
- There is no explanation for the universe's existence.
- This means that no purpose for the universe can be identified, whether ontologically (ie. none exists) or epistemologically (ie. we can never find out).
- A will beyond the universe does not exist.
- If "purpose" comes from a "will", and there is no "purpose", then there is no "will".

span.style: font-size: 11px;

div.span: - We've previously identified an intelligent will beyond the universe by connecting "reality is ordered" (despite "reality tends to progress to disorder" and "reality could have been different") to "intelligence correlates with purpose/consciousness".

span.style: font-size: 11px;

div.span: - If these inferences are grounded in phenomenological awareness of your own will, intelligence, and pattern recognition (of the same effects in reality's structure), then this argument also must commit to the rejection of your own will, the link between intelligence and order, and/or the process itself of defining reality's structure from pattern recognition.

font.b: How the Project Addresses These Commitments

div.font: - "No purpose for the universe can be identified", and "t

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: here is no will beyond the universe."

div.font: - The inferences in this project can be used to identify universal purpose, so this claim requires proof (ie. identifying the invalid inference/deduction and supplying an alternative that fits reality more encompassingly).
- "I reject the identification of my own will, the link between intelligence and order, or the idea that I can accurately define reality from my own awareness."

span.style: font-size: 11px;

div.span: - If you reject phenomenological awareness of your own will - something that is felt/known, not argued - then you lack the capacity to identify others in reality.

span.style: font-size: 11px;
span.font: - If you don't recognize the link between your own intelligence and order, then an external will can never be used to abductively explain reality's order.

span.style: font-size: 11px;

div.span: - If you reject the process of defining reality itself, then see the Cost of Disagreement section in the project's conclusion for further commitments.
